summary.headline: Birlasoft Q2 FY27 revenue rose 2.1% QoQ to $148.3M, EBITDA margin held at 15.2%, but management says order book fell short of expectations.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 2.1% QoQ in constant currency and dollar terms to $148.3M (INR1,416.2 crore, +2.7% QoQ in rupees). EBITDA was INR215.3 crore (15.2% margin), absorbing about 170 bps of wage-revision impact from July 2026 and investments in sales and service-line capability. Deal signings were $116.1M TCV in Q2 (+9% YoY), with H1 at $285M (+15% YoY), but management said some deals slipped into Q3/Q4 and it was not pleased with order booking. Management said H2 financial performance should beat H1, while declining to give formal guidance.

financial_highlights.change: +2.1% QoQ in USD and cc; +2.7% QoQ in INR
E&U soft due to ramp-down at one European client

segments.name: Manufacturing
segments.commentary: Grew 5.2% QoQ, the fastest vertical in Q2; management expects directional growth to continue with new logos coming in.

segments.name: BFSI
segments.commentary: Grew 3.6% QoQ; Q3 expected slightly soft on furloughs, with management bullish on structural growth from Q4.

segments.name: Life Sciences & Services
segments.commentary: Grew 2.1% QoQ; margins dropped in Q2 due to one program, with management expecting recovery from Q4.

segments.name: E&U
segments.commentary: Soft due to ramp-down of work for one European client; management does not expect further downside but sees no near-term bounce back, with turnaround expected over 2-3 quarters.

guidance_outlook: Management does not give formal guidance but expects H2 FY27 financial performance to be better than H1.
Q4 FY27 expected to be the strongest quarter QoQ if order execution happens between now and January/February; no sharp Q4 dip seen as of today.
EBITDA margin expected to stay around 15%, with seasonal ups and downs; catch-up expected over next couple of quarters to offset wage increase.
Furloughs in Q3 expected to be in the same range as last year.
Continued investment in sales and tech capabilities; management says margin upside will be reinvested.
capex_capacity: Reinvestment in tech infrastructure driving higher depreciation and amortization and higher PPE on balance sheet; expected to continue for a while.
Office refurbishment and moves to better offices adding to D&A.
Other intangibles rising YoY as some capability investments are amortised under accounting guidelines.
Utilisation rose to a multi-quarter high; management says it will remain steady and will not return to prior 85-86% levels.
Management says about 90% of sales and capability investment work is already done.
demand_pricing: Management says the demand environment is unchanged versus Q1: steady, not worsening, not improving.
Q2 order intake was soft because some deals slipped into Q3 and Q4; no deals reported as lost.
Net new deal intake remains the key concern; management says pipeline has risen slightly and AI-related conversations are increasing.
Pricing pressure is seen in competitive deals but not broadly across the mid-market.
Around one-third of code is now generated by Agentic AI tools, up from about 25% a few months earlier; machine-written code rose 10% QoQ.

qa_highlights.question: Has the exit from low-margin accounts been completed, and is annuity revenue rising?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says the exit from negative accounts is done and dusted; annuity business is rising and revenue quality is improving.

qa_highlights.question: Was Q2 revenue in line with expectations, and what drove the EBITDA margin walk?
qa_highlights.answer: Q2 revenue was in line with plan; order book fell short. Wage hike cost about 170 bps QoQ, partly offset by operating efficiencies and better revenue quality.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Q4 expected to be stronger after the past two years' dips?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says prior Q4 dips came from client surprises; as of today it sees no sharp Q4 dip and expects Q4 to be the strongest quarter if orders are executed by January/February.

qa_highlights.question: What explains the other expenses increase of roughly 7-8% QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Complementary workforce rose by about 50 resources for clients needing niche skills at short notice; the increase was matched by revenue uptick.

qa_highlights.question: Is E&U likely to recover and could the client ramp down further?
qa_highlights.answer: Management calls the E&U decline a one-time event, not structural; it expects E&U to turn around over the next 2-3 quarters, and declined to give client specifics.

qa_highlights.question: Why did PPE and intangibles rise sharply YoY?
qa_highlights.answer: Tech infrastructure refresh over recent quarters drove PPE up; some capability investments are being amortised, which lifted intangibles.

risks_watch: Order intake: management itself is not satisfied with bookings; H2 signings are needed to support FY28 growth.
E&U: further ramp-down risk at the European client; no near-term rebound expected.
Margin: wage revision and continued sales investment may keep EBITDA near 15% rather than expanding; seasonal Q3 softness.
Q3 furloughs and possible client surprises that could repeat last year's Q4 dip.
Rising D&A from tech infrastructure and office refurbishment; surplus cash deployment plan not yet announced.
summary.management_tone: Confident on execution and H2 revenue and cash, but notably cautious and self-critical on order booking; management repeatedly declined to give formal guidance and stressed that the turnaround is not yet secured.
key_quotes: But quite frankly, on the order book, I think we did not do a good job. I mean, we expected ourselves to do better.
I don't believe that we have turned the corner around yet. I think we have got a lot more work to do.
Now as far as getting out of negative accounts, I think that job is done and over.
And this is within the range we had indicated earlier.

growth.why: No formal guidance; management expects H2 FY27 better than H1 and Q4 strongest, with EBITDA margin around 15%, but backing is vague as order book fell short with deals slipping into Q3/Q4 and no capacity additions quantified.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: EBITDA margin guided around 15% with a catch-up expected over the next couple of quarters to offset the ~170 bps wage hike, but management says any upside will be reinvested in sales and tech, so expansion is not assured.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Reinvestment in tech infrastructure is raising PPE and D&A, but no new capacity is quantified; about 90% of sales and capability investment work is already done.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Q2 revenue rose 2.1% QoQ to $148.3M and Q4 is expected to be the strongest quarter, but order intake fell short with deals slipping into Q3/Q4 and H1 TCV was $285M (+15% YoY).

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation rose to a multi-quarter high but management says it will stay steady and not return to 85-86%; the surplus cash deployment plan is not yet announced, and the capex discussed is capability spending already largely done.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management gave no formal guidance and stressed the turnaround is not yet secured; order book fell short of expectations and demand is steady, not improving.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Net new deal intake is the key concern, with deals slipping into Q3/Q4, Q3 BFSI expected slightly soft on furloughs, and E&U still weak for the next 2-3 quarters.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: No new product, brand or model launches were discussed; the AI tooling mentioned is internal code generation.

rows.label: H2 order intake recovery
rows.why: Q2 TCV was $116.1M (+9% YoY) and H1 was $285M (+15% YoY), but management is dissatisfied with bookings and pipeline has only risen slightly; H2 signings are needed to support FY28 growth.

rows.label: E&U recovery after European client ramp-down
rows.why: E&U fell on a ramp-down at one European client; management expects no further downside and a turnaround over 2-3 quarters, but sees no near-term bounce back.

rows.label: Collections and DSO at a 2-year best
rows.why: Collections were $164M and DSO fell to 51 days, a 2-year best, with cash and equivalents of $300.4M as of 30 Sep 2026.

tone.note: Management was confident on H2 revenue, Q4 seasonality, cash and collections, and the E&U and margin recovery, but was self-critical about order booking and declined to give formal guidance; the Q&A focused on order intake, E&U and the other-expense rise.
